name: Potiphar's wife
charge: Soliciting her husband's servant day by day, and bearing false witness against him when he fled
summary: She asked Joseph to lie with her and he refused, telling her it would be a great wickedness and a sin against God. When she caught him by the garment and he left it in her hand and fled, she kept the garment and turned it into evidence against him. The record gives her offense and the statute it breaks, and never gives her sentence.
offense: His master's wife cast her eyes upon Joseph and said, Lie with me (Genesis 39:7), and she spake to Joseph day by day, and he hearkened not unto her (Genesis 39:10), so the solicitation was sustained and not a moment's impulse. His refusal names the offense before any law was written at Sinai: there is none greater in this house than I, neither hath he kept back any thing from me but thee, because thou art his wife; how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God (Genesis 39:9). Adultery was known to be sin from the beginning. Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws (Genesis 26:5), and even a heathen king rebuked Isaac on the same ground, one of the people might lightly have lien with thy wife, and thou shouldest have brought guiltiness upon us (Genesis 26:10), so the nations themselves knew it carried guilt. Then, on a day when none of the men of the house were within, she caught him by his garment, and he left it in her hand  and fled (Genesis 39:11-12), which is the example the wise man commands: flee from sin as from the face of a serpent, for if thou comest too near it, it will bite thee, the teeth  thereof are as the teeth of a lion (Ecclesiasticus (Sirach) 21:2). The solicitation was followed by false witness. She called the men of her house and said, he hath brought in an Hebrew unto us to mock us, he came in unto me to lie with me, and I cried with a loud voice, and she laid up the garment by her until his lord came home (Genesis 39:14-16). The same mouth that had flattered him turned and accused him: the lips of a strange woman drop as an honeycomb, and her mouth is smoother than oil, but her end is bitter as wormwood, and her ways are moveable (Proverbs 5:3-6), and more bitter than death is the woman whose heart is snares and nets, and her hands as bands, whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her (Ecclesiastes 7:26). The later law requires diligent inquiry and directs that a false witness receive the consequence intended for the accused (Deuteronomy 19:16-19). That statute identifies the gravity of false accusation; Genesis does not say an Israelite court applied it in Egypt.
judgment: The judgment recorded falls on the innocent man. His master's wrath was kindled, and he took Joseph and put him into the prison, a place where the king's prisoners were bound (Genesis 39:19-20). No inquiry or hearing of Joseph's defence is described. Proverbs warns of the force of a husband's jealousy: jealousy is the rage of a man, therefore he will not spare in the day of vengeance, he will not regard any ransom (Proverbs 6:34-35). Against the woman no later sentence is recorded. Her offense is double under the law, the solicitation and then the false witness, and both stand written with no penalty set against them. What the record does report is where the favour went: the Lord was with Joseph, and shewed him mercy, and gave him favour in the sight of the keeper of the prison (Genesis 39:21), and the psalm carries it on, whose feet they hurt with fetters, he was laid in iron, until the time that his word came, the word of the Lord tried him (Psalms 105:18-19). The prison became part of the road to government, but Joseph's eventual deliverance did not make the accusation true.

entries.commentary: The Lord was with Joseph in his captivity, and his master saw that the Lord made all that he did to prosper; Potiphar made him overseer over his house, and the Lord blessed the Egyptian's house for Joseph's sake. The Most High deals with His people even in captivity and gives them compassion before them who carried them captive; the favor on Joseph is the pattern of that prayer.

His master's wife cast her eyes upon Joseph and said, Lie with me; and he refused: how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God? Adultery was known as sin from the beginning, long before Sinai. Abraham kept the commandments, statutes, and laws; and Abimelech rebuked Isaac because one of the people might have lain with his wife and brought guiltiness upon them. The nations themselves knew adultery brought guilt.

She spake to Joseph day by day, and he hearkened not. Then she arranged the empty house, caught him by his garment, and he left his garment in her hand and fled. That is the example: flee from sin as from the face of a serpent, for if thou comest too near it, it will bite thee; the teeth thereof are as the teeth of a lion. Joseph knew thirty more seconds of entertaining her would be the bite.

When she saw he was fled, she lied and cried that the Hebrew came in to mock her, holding his garment as evidence. The scriptures warn of that spirit: the woman whose heart is snares and nets and her hands as bands; whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her. The lips of a strange woman drop as an honeycomb, but her end is bitter, and her ways are moveable; the same mouth that flattered turns and accuses.

When his master heard the words of his wife, his wrath was kindled and he put Joseph into the prison. He did not seek understanding, for jealousy is the rage of a man: he will not spare in the day of vengeance, nor regard any ransom.

But the Lord was with Joseph, and shewed him mercy, and gave him favour in the sight of the keeper of the prison, and everything in the prison was committed to Joseph's hand. Everywhere Joseph went the favor followed, because the Most High was ordering his steps the whole way, so that Joseph would stand where he could save the whole house of Israel alive. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant)

An image in itself is not the sin, except for that white image of the beast; making images to bow down to them and serve them is the transgression, for the Lord thy God is a jealous God. Visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation: Israel is yet this day in captivity, scattered for a reproach and a curse, according to all the iniquities of the fathers which departed from the Lord. Right now Israel is paying for the sins of the fathers; that is why the people are scattered to the four corners of the earth.

And shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments. Judith recounted how the Most High tried the fathers for the examination of their hearts: he tried Abraham and Isaac, and Jacob in Mesopotamia of Syria keeping the sheep of Laban, serving twenty years with his wages changed and given Leah when he looked for Rachel. In Judith's day there was no tribe, family, people, nor city that worshipped gods made with hands, as had been aforetime; for that cause she trusted the Lord would not despise the nation. Mercy rests on them that know none other God, not Allah, not Buddha, not a white Jesus.

Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy. The word says remember because Israel would forget it: in this captivity the people were forced to serve other gods and their religions, and the Sabbath was lost through forced conversion. Look up the blue laws, also known as Sunday laws; they help give understanding of why the Bible says remember the Sabbath day.

An altar of stone was not to be built of hewn stone, for lifting up a tool upon it pollutes it; neither go up by steps unto the altar, that thy nakedness be not discovered thereon. This scripture helps explain pants, precept upon precept. The priests were given linen breeches to cover their nakedness from the loins even unto the thighs when they came near the altar, and Israel was called in this same reading to be a kingdom of priests, so do not be simple and say that law was only for Aaron and his sons. Those breeches were made for men and not for women, as the law of the garments also shows.

When the Most High cut off the nations of the land of Canaan, the Canaanites, the Jebusites, the Perizzites, and the Girgashites, and Israel succeeded them and dwelt in their cities and houses, Israel was to separate three cities in the midst of the land and prepare the way to them. This law goes into accidental death, what the Bible sometimes calls manslaughter. An Israelite who accidentally killed another could flee to one of these three cities of refuge, where the avenger of blood could not seek him out and kill him there to revenge the blood of his nearest of kin.

Whoso killeth his neighbour ignorantly, whom he hated not in time past, means he did not mean to do it; it was an accident. The example given is two men hewing wood, and the axe head slips from the helve and strikes the neighbour that he die: he shall flee to one of those cities and live. The avenger of blood is the nearest of kin, and while his heart is hot he may pursue and overtake the slayer because the way is long. But the slayer was not worthy of death, because he hated him not in time past; there was no premeditation, no intention to kill. Accidents happen, and the Most High put laws in place for when these things happened. If it was for sure an accident, the man is not worthy of death, as the scripture says.

If the Lord enlarge thy coast as he sware unto the fathers, then three more cities were to be added. As Israel grew and possessed more of the land of Canaan, more cities of refuge were established where a slayer could flee from the avenger of blood. The purpose is stated plainly: that innocent blood be not shed in the land which the Lord giveth thee for an inheritance, and so blood be upon thee.

This gives the distinction between an accident and intentional killing; this is describing murder. He hated his neighbour and lay in wait for him: he devised a scheme, waited for the right opportunity and the right time, rose up against him, and smote him mortally that he died. The murderer cannot then run to a city of refuge to lay low. Those cities were not established for him; they were established so retaliation did not come on those who accidentally brought harm to somebody. The elders of his own city shall fetch him from there and deliver him into the hand of the avenger of blood, that he may die. Thine eye shall not pity him: putting away the guilt of innocent blood from Israel is what makes it go well with the nation.

What is a landmark? It pays to use tools outside the scriptures, because what good is reading the Bible without understanding of the words written in it. The Zondervan Bible Dictionary defines a landmark as an object, stone, or post used to mark the boundary of a field, and notes that removal of landmarks was prohibited by the Mosaic law. The landmark establishes the boundaries of a man's property, where it begins and where it ends. A man who keeps nudging his neighbour's landmark over little by little until he has taken an acre is stealing land; the dictionary notes it was considered equal to theft.

One witness shall not rise up against a man for any iniquity or any sin. One man alone saying he saw a theft is not proof; anybody can come and lie and get people put to death, imprisoned, or beaten. At the mouth of two witnesses, or at the mouth of three witnesses, shall the matter be established. It has to be clear-cut; two or three solid witnesses, not one solid witness and a shaky witness. We deal with facts.

When a false witness rises up, both men in the controversy stand before the Lord, before the priests and the judges of those days. False accusation is real: people will lie on a man to cover themselves, and false witnesses arise among your own people as well, which is part of why the nation fell into captivity. The judges shall make diligent inquisition: they get to the bottom of the matter and find out exactly who is telling the truth, who is lying, and what the facts are. A judge cannot judge a matter off what one person says; each side tells the story in his own favour, so you must examine the whole matter, question both sides against each other, and decipher the truth. Diligent inquisition is what separates a good judge from a bad judge; a lazy or partial judge makes false judgment. If the witness is found false, then shall ye do unto him as he had thought to have done unto his brother. Accuse a man falsely of stealing, and the judgment for stealing comes on you; accuse him falsely of adultery or another sin punishable by death, and you are put to death, because that is what you intended for your neighbour. So is evil put away from Israel.
The judgment is public and it teaches: those which remain shall hear and fear, and shall henceforth commit no more any such evil among you.

Thine eye shall not pity: in this time under Moses it was life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot. If a man knocked out your tooth, the recompense was exact, and it went through the judges one way or another; thus saith the law. Christ spoke on this saying, because exact retaliation between men creates a never-ending cycle of vengeance and hatred. Turning the other cheek does not mean letting somebody beat you down into the dirt; it means when somebody does something to you, do not come back later seeking revenge. Seeking revenge only brings more judgment on your own head; the wise course is to let it go and let the Most High repay, for vengeance belongs to him.

Give thanks unto the Most High, call upon His name, and make known His deeds among the people. Sing unto Him, glory in His holy name, and let the heart of them that seek Him rejoice; seek His face forevermore. Remember His marvelous works, His wonders, and the judgments of His mouth. The Bible tells us to remember our past. -

O seed of Abraham and children of Jacob His chosen: the Most High is our God and His judgments are in all the earth. He has remembered His covenant forever, the word commanded to a thousand generations, made with Abraham, sworn to Isaac, confirmed to Jacob for a law and to Israel for an everlasting covenant. If Israel was to have an everlasting covenant, then the new covenant cannot suddenly involve all people. You must ask these questions of anyone who does not use the scriptures.

When they were few and strangers in the land, He suffered no man to wrong them and reproved kings for their sake: touch not mine anointed. He called a famine and sent a man before them, even Joseph, sold for a servant and bound with fetters until his word came to pass. The king loosed him and made him lord of his house and ruler of his substance, to bind his princes and teach his senators wisdom. Our forefather Joseph taught the Egyptians; those who boast in Egyptology forget our forefathers taught them. -

Israel came into Egypt and Jacob sojourned in the land of Ham; He increased His people and made them stronger than their enemies, then turned the Egyptians' hearts to hate them. He sent Moses and Aaron who showed His signs and wonders in the land of Ham; He recounts the plagues of darkness, blood, frogs, flies, lice, hail, fire, and locusts. The locusts and caterpillars devoured all the herbs and fruit of the ground; this is the devourer, and the Most High promises to rebuke the devourer for the sake of a righteous nation. He smote all the firstborn, the chief of all their strength. The firstborn is the chief of one's strength, as Reuben was Jacob's strength before he lost it. -

He brought Israel out with silver and gold, and there was not one feeble person among the tribes; look at the sicknesses we suffer now under the curses. He spread a cloud for a covering and fire for light, brought quails and the bread of heaven, and opened the rock so the waters gushed out in the dry place. He gave them the lands of the heathen and the labor of the people, that they might keep His statutes and laws. But we were not thankful, we went into idolatry, and now we are scattered in Babylon in America. -

verses.text: And it came to pass after these things, that his master’s wife cast her eyes upon Joseph; and she said, Lie with me.
But he refused, and said unto his master’s wife, Behold, my master wotteth not what is with me in the house, and he hath committed all that he hath to my hand;
There is none greater in this house than I; neither hath he kept back any thing from me but thee, because thou art his wife: how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?
And it came to pass, as she spake to Joseph day by day, that he hearkened not unto her, to lie by her, or to be with her.
And it came to pass about this time, that Joseph went into the house to do his business; and there was none of the men of the house there within.
And she caught him by his garment, saying, Lie with me: and he left his garment in her hand, and fled, and got him out.
And it came to pass, when she saw that he had left his garment in her hand, and was fled forth,
That she called unto the men of her house, and spake unto them, saying, See, he hath brought in an Hebrew unto us to mock us; he came in unto me to lie with me, and I cried with a loud voice:
And it came to pass, when he heard that I lifted up my voice and cried, that he left his garment with me, and fled, and got him out.
And she laid up his garment by her, until his lord came home.
And she spake unto him according to these words, saying, The Hebrew servant, which thou hast brought unto us, came in unto me to mock me:
And it came to pass, as I lifted up my voice and cried, that he left his garment with me, and fled out.
And it came to pass, when his master heard the words of his wife, which she spake unto him, saying, After this manner did thy servant to me; that his wrath was kindled.
And Joseph’s master took him, and put him into the prison, a place where the king’s prisoners were bound: and he was there in the prison.
Thou shalt not commit adultery.
Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour.
If a false witness rise up against any man to testify against him that which is wrong;
Then both the men, between whom the controversy is, shall stand before the Lord, before the priests and the judges, which shall be in those days;
And the judges shall make diligent inquisition: and, behold, if the witness be a false witness, and hath testified falsely against his brother;
Then shall ye do unto him, as he had thought to have done unto his brother: so shalt thou put the evil away from among you.
He sent a man before them, even Joseph, who was sold for a servant:
Whose feet they hurt with fetters: he was laid in iron:
Until the time that his word came: the word of the Lord tried him.
